patch.value: GH-1753: the triage projection advertises an output cursor that is stale on unchanged replay (read_output_cursor_stale)

Reported in GH-1753 against 2026.11.18. A budget-driven second projection of the list triage delivery step advertises a continuation whose replay, against identical rows and options, is refused with read_output_cursor_stale. The reporter's in-memory fixture of 43 synthetic rows (output budget 1000 TOON tokens, limit 30, output limit 100) replays cleanly with filter padding 134 and 138, but padding 136 delivers 12 rows and the advertised cursor is refused. This follows the composed amount and token ceilings work and the producer next_cursor clipping fix, both related.

Replaying the advertised cursor of a budget-driven second triage projection against unchanged rows and options resumes after the last delivered row; A changed source still refuses the cursor with read_output_cursor_stale; Coverage includes the second-projection case and the adjacent passing paddings as controls
An output cursor from the first response resumes after its last delivered row when the same query and item data are replayed; the stale refusal remains only for a changed source.
With filter padding 136 the first response delivers 12 rows and advertises a cursor that the unchanged replay refuses with read_output_cursor_stale; paddings 134 and 138 replay successfully.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Root cause (reproduced on src with the reporter fixture: padding 134 resumes at demo-12, 136 refuses with read_output_cursor_stale, 138 resumes at demo-11). Two defects combine.
(1) Fixpoint drift. The read-output stage compacts rows while measuring the envelope with the intent receipt's earlier estimate (989). After it returns, the intent receipt is re-settled to the delivered estimate (1000, then 1001), which adds a digit and pushes the settled envelope one token over the 1000-token budget it was compacted to.
(2) Unreplayable binding. attachReadOutputContracts then projects again with the measured overhead charged. The intent pass keeps 21 rows instead of 22, and the output cursor is bound to that 21-row collection (n=21 and its fingerprint). A replay's first pass charges no overhead, keeps 22 rows, and so never matches.
Fix (1): the intent layer registers an estimate mirror for each read-output pass (registerReadOutputPassHooks, keyed by the exact options object finalizeReadOutputEnvelope hands to applyReadOutputDimensions, through an internal WeakMap in read-output-budget.ts, so no public SDK surface changes). updateReadOutputReceiptEstimate settles it inside every fixpoint, so compaction measures the intent receipt's final estimate_tokens digits and within_budget flag.
Fix (2): the charged second pass registers the first pass's projection as continuationBinding. applyReadOutputContinuation validates the cursor against the bound collection and slices the delivered one; captureReadOutputContinuationState issues total_rows and the fingerprint from the bound collection. Backward (tail-retention) collections keep their own rows.
Evidence: a brute-force replay harness over 1,476 configurations (toon/json x output/token/both spellings x budgets 700/1000/1400 x title lengths x paddings 100..180) went from 2 stale cursors to 0, and every one of the 360 cursor chains pages contiguously. Recharges still run (189 in a 4-variant grid), but none now coincides with an output cursor, so the binding is a structural guarantee covered by a direct spec. Negative controls: without the mirror, the reporter, sweep and changed-source specs fail; without the binding, the direct binding spec fails.

value.text: Review (Codex, uncommitted diff): mirroring the intent receipt's within_budget flag inside the fixpoint made a JSON triage page with outputRowContract (300-character title) that fits exactly at 490 tokens settle at 491 and be omitted. An oversized start writes "false", one byte longer than "true", which yields a second, self-consistent fixpoint. Fixed by mirroring only estimated_tokens: the flag keeps the intent pass's value while candidates are measured, an accepted candidate fits, and the final reconcileIntentFit only ever clears the flag. A spec pins the exact-fit page (1 row, 490 tokens, within_budget true). Negative control: restoring the flag mirror fails it. The replay harness still shows 0 stale cursors and 360/360 contiguous chains.

value.text: Review round 2 (Codex, uncommitted diff): once GH-1754 compacted cursor-named custom fields, an intent output cursor fingerprinted the compacted text, so an equal-length edit in an omitted suffix replayed without being refused. The same blind spot already held on HEAD for every intent-compacted field, a long title for example, against the documented guarantee that same-cardinality content changes fail closed. Fixed generally: intentContinuationBinding binds every intent read's output cursors to the producer's uncompacted rows, cut to the prefix the first intent pass kept. Both passes register that binding through the read-output pass hooks, which replaces the earlier recharge-only binding. A replay rebuilds exactly these rows, so an unchanged source still replays and the charged second pass keeps issuing cursors a replay accepts. A new spec refuses an equal-length edit in the omitted suffix of both a compacted title and a compacted sync_cursor, and the unchanged control replays; removing the binding fails it. The replay harness still shows 0 stale and 360/360 contiguous chains, and the 44 affected spec files pass. Also per review (P3): each fix now has a runnable linked test (pm test --run) and the contract doc is linked through pm docs.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round 3 (Codex): the read-output layer re-applied the caller's include projection to a binding built from the raw producer result. That result has no context_intent and no budget_derived_limit, so pm list --for triage --output-include context_intent failed with an unknown selector. Fixed: the binding is now the delivered intent envelope, and only the top-level row collections the intent cut to a prefix are replaced by the producer's uncompacted rows of that prefix. A collection the intent lengthened, such as warnings with an appended limit warning, keeps its delivered rows. A new spec covers --output-include context_intent and a row-field projection (items.id,items.title) whose cursor replays. Negative control: a raw-source binding fails it. The harness still shows 360/360 chains.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round 4 (Codex): captureReadOutputContinuationState hashed every continuation collection eagerly. HEAD did the same over the compacted rows, but hashing the uncompacted binding added work to reads that fit and issue no cursor, and it threw RangeError on an SDK row holding an invalid Date. Fixed: each collection's fingerprint is a memoized getter, computed only when buildReadOutputContinuation issues a cursor; validating an incoming cursor already hashed lazily. Spec: a string-compacted one-row triage read whose row holds new Date(NaN) returns its row with no truncation. Negative control: eager hashing throws Invalid time value.

patch.value: The reporter fixture resumes at paddings 134, 136 and 138 (136 now delivers 11 rows and resumes at demo-11); a replay harness over 1,476 configurations went from 2 stale cursors to 0 with 360/360 contiguous chains; changed and same-length hidden edits still refuse with read_output_cursor_stale
Replaying the advertised cursor of a budget-driven second triage projection against unchanged rows resumes after the last delivered row; a changed source still refuses with read_output_cursor_stale

Two causes, both fixed. (1) The read-output fixpoint now settles the intent receipt's estimated_tokens through a per-pass estimate mirror (registerReadOutputPassHooks), so row compaction measures the digits that receipt finally carries; the page no longer settles one token over its budget, which had forced a charged second pass. (2) Every intent read binds its output cursors to the delivered envelope with each prefix-cut top-level row collection replaced by the producer's uncompacted rows of the first pass's prefix. A replay rebuilds exactly that collection, a charged second pass still issues cursors a replay accepts, string compaction cannot hide an equal-length edit, and include selectors resolve as on the delivered envelope. Fingerprints are computed only when a continuation is issued.
An intent read's advertised output cursor replays against unchanged rows: compaction measures the intent receipt's final estimate, and cursors bind to the uncompacted rows the first pass keeps

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
PR #1758 review (CodeRabbit, major), declined with evidence. The claim: a replay whose own charged pass keeps a shorter prefix than the binding slices the shorter collection, so rows between the two prefix ends are withheld without an output cursor. That path needs a replay whose settled envelope exceeds its intent budget.
(a) Under the canonical --output-budget spelling, the read-output stage now settles within the same budget (estimate mirror), so no recharge accompanies an output cursor: 0 in the 1,476-configuration grid, the session grids, and outputRowContract and pretty-JSON variants.
(b) Under the legacy --token-budget spelling, no output cursor is issued at all: 0 across list, search and next, 9 budgets, 3 title lengths and 13 paddings.
(c) Even then, for list and search the charged intent pass rebases the producer next_cursor to its last kept row (compactPaginatedContextIntentRows), so the withheld tail stays advertised through --after.
A guard for an unreachable branch could not be covered under the 100% exact-coverage gate, so none is added. If a future overhead makes recharge and cursor coincide, the fix belongs where the charge is decided.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review of the PR #1758 head (base main) found two more issues, both fixed.
(P2) A cursor issued by 2026.11.19 fingerprinted the intent-compacted rows, so after an upgrade the raw-row binding refused it as stale on unchanged data. continuationMatches in read-output/continuation.ts now falls back to the delivered rows' fingerprint when a binding is present. That fallback accepts only a cursor bound to those rows, so hidden-edit detection for current cursors is unchanged. Verified with a real cursor issued by main's build (the branch replay resumes at demo-5), plus a synthetic legacy-cursor spec; a changed source still refuses both cursor kinds.
(P3) When the intent compacted strings, hashing raw SDK rows threw RangeError on an invalid Date. Main hashed the walked copy, in which a Date becomes a plain record. The binding rows now take the same walk without string compaction (normalizeContextIntentValue). A spec pages and replays compacted rows that hold a Date and an array.
Negative controls fail without each fix. The sweep spec was cut to 44 configurations with an explicit 120 s timeout after it timed out under coverage instrumentation, keeping a non-vacuity floor of 20 followed chains and 0 omissions. Targeted coverage over all six touched files is complete, and the 1,476-configuration harness still shows 360/360 chains.
